reviewer: rig_translations agent, independent from wind/mooring author
method: Opened German sailing-lexicon entries independently and checked each label against SVG source coordinates in content/day-skipper/src/figures.py. The sailtraining PDF was retrieved directly and its nautical glossary read with pdftotext after the web parser failed. This is semantic review; root performs rendered layout verification.

texts.reason: The two arrows run from x=20 toward x=234/194, showing moving air. Wind is the same nautical noun in German.
The arrow approaches the boat from the left, so the left label correctly identifies the wind-facing side as Luv.
Windseite paraphrases the wind-facing side immediately below Luv; its placement fixes which side it means.
Dem Wind zugewandt states the defining direction of Luv; weather side here has no meteorological-forecast meaning.
The right-hand side lies downstream of the left-to-right airflow, so Lee is the correct nautical direction.
Vom Wind abgewandt gives the defining leeward direction. It does not incorrectly promise complete shelter.
The boom path extends from (260,158) to (336,170) before the heel rotation, thus into the right-hand lee side. Hier correctly limits the statement to this drawing.
The shore drawn near x=430–498 is downwind of the boat near x=260. Küste in Lee preserves that boat-relative hazard.
With airflow to the right and land to the right, wind carries the boat toward land. The direction and grounding implication are correct.
The shore near x=14–60 is upwind of the boat. Küste in Luv preserves weather shore as viewed from the boat.
At the left-hand coast the arrows blow from land toward the water. Omitting the unconditional shelter promise improves precision without reversing direction.

cap.reason: The source construction explicitly uses an astern view. A positive 16-degree SVG rotation tilts the mast right, away from the left-to-right wind, so the boat krängt nach Lee.

texts.reason: The three protective cushions sit between hull and berth. German Fender is also the plural form used here.
The glossary defines Querleine as a transverse line from amidships to shore or another ship. The red path (300,150) to (300,206) is perpendicular to the hull axis.
The line leads straight toward the pontoon at y=214 and opposes motion away from it. Querab names this transverse direction.
The line starts at the stern (122,140) and reaches the aft shore cleat (60,206). Achterleine matches both origin and lead.
The stern line decreases x from 122 to 60. With the bow to the right this is from the stern aft, exactly vom Heck nach achtern.
The forward mooring line runs from (472,96) to (520,206). Vorleine names a bow mooring line; it is not the bowline knot Palstek.
The bow line increases x from 472 to 520, so it leads forward from the right-hand bow. Vom Bug nach vorn is correct.
The line originates forward at (440,110) and leads aft to (210,206). Vorspring is named for its forward onboard origin.
The forward green path decreases x from 440 to 210, confirming vom Bug nach achtern rather than the reverse.
Moving the boat forward increases the length demanded of this aft-leading spring. It therefore restrains forward surge: Vorrutschen.
The other green line originates aft at (150,144) and leads forward to (380,206). Achterspring is the correct name.
This path increases x from 150 to 380. With the stern at left, vom Heck nach vorn describes its geometry correctly.
Moving the boat aft lengthens this forward-leading spring. It therefore restrains backward surge: Zurückrutschen.
